svg.text: RÖDALM daily dash: power and battery-sense wiring
rev 1, plan · Waveshare e-Paper ESP32 Driver Board (Rev 3) · Adafruit bq25185 #6091 · 694449 2000 mAh pouch · same parts as stand-4.2in
GPIO 4 gates the panel rail, not free
4.5 V on USB · ≈ cell on battery
GND (one net with BATT − and DC-in −)
on the carrier, at the pin
Charger GND, BATT −, DC-in − and LOAD −
are one net through the charger.

text.tspan: 1. Tap the charger's BAT monitor pad. Never LOAD, never the driver's 5V pin: those sit at 4.5 V
whenever USB is in, so the panel would read "full" for as long as it is plugged in.
2. R1 at the charger, R2 + C1 at the pin. The long wire can then pass at most 42 µA into a short,
and C1 holds the high-impedance tap steady for the ADC's sampling capacitor.
3. R2 and C1 go to the driver's GND pin. Never to the cell's own tabs: the pack's protection
PCB sits in the negative leg, so the raw tab is not the system's ground.
4. 4.20 V reads 2.10 V at GPIO 35, 3.60 V reads 1.80 V. That stays inside the 12 dB range
(accurate to ≈ 2.45 V). The divider draws 21 µA, about 0.5 mAh a day, ~1 % of the 2 mA idle.
5.0 V reads 3.00 V at GPIO 34; 4.75–5.25 V reads 2.85–3.15 V.
That is a clean logic high (needs 2.48 V) and never above 3.3 V.
GPIO 34 has no internal pulls, so R4 is what holds it low.
It is an RTC pin, so plugging in can wake the board.
The firmware can then report "charging", stay awake on USB
for OTA, and make a low-battery cutoff recoverable.
Charge current: set 1 A. At the 500 mA default the 6 h safety
timer can stop a flat 2000 mAh cell before it is full.

svg.text: Header J3 on the driver (Rev 3 schematic): SVP 3 · IO34 5 · IO35 6 · IO32 7 · 5V 19. Resistors 1 %. Wire: 26 AWG silicone for power, 28–30 AWG for the sense lines.
